newsitem.title: ITALY: Owner says Italy's Il Giorno daily paper to close.
newsitem.headline: Owner says Italy's Il Giorno daily paper to close.

text.p: Milan-based daily newspaper Il Giorno is to close after potential buyers wanted a higher contribution to shore up the loss-making broadsheet than its owner Sogedit was prepared to give, Sogedit said on Friday.

Il Giorno, which costs 1,500 lire (95 cents) a copy and has a circulation of 90,000 mainly in the northern regions of Lombardy and Piemonte, is being placed in liquidation along with graphics company Nuova Same Spa.
Sogedit, which is part of the state-controlled energy group Eni, said it had valued the contribution it was prepared to make in any sale at 58 billion lire.
"The final offers presented totalled a much higher cost," it said in a statement without naming potential purchasers.
Reports this week said Eni was close to selling the loss-making paper to New Day srl, a consortium headed by a former director general of state broadcaster RAI.
New Day was reported to have offered 25 billion with Sogedit covering forecast losses of up to 65 billion for 1997 and 1998.

Il Giorno began in the 1950s and was bought by Eni's then chairman, Enrico Mattei, shortly after its start. It was the first Italian newspaper to have a separate economic news section, a women's page and to use colour.
Eni, which had sought a taker for the daily for a while, has poured more than one trillion lire into it since its purchase.
Several Italian papers have closed in recent years in an increasingly competitive market in which the major papers regularly offer inserts as a way of attracting readers.

The National Federation of the Italian Press said in a statement it was unthinkable to shut down a paper which had played such an important role in the Italian media "as if it were shutting down a petrol pump".
The federation said the closure reduced "the already poor pluralism of information in the daily press" and called for a the government to intervene.
It asked for a meeting with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, adding the journalists' trade union would not accept a closure lying down. ($1=1,565 lire)
